anomaly_def.Name: Schema and Index Design Anomaly + CPU Resource Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
Schema and Index Design Anomaly : Physical data-model and indexing choices mismatch workload access paths, forcing otherwise correct SQL to read or write far more data than necessary.
CPU Resource Anomaly : Host CPU cores become saturated by database processes, throttling all sessions regardless of their individual efficiency.

When these root causes strike together, the system displays a blend of I/O-heavy access paths and persistent CPU saturation. Execution plans show full scans, large hash or sort operations, and repeated key lookups, while OS metrics report high run-queue depth, elevated context switches, and spikes in CPU time for the most frequent statements. Latency escalates non-linearly: queries slowed by scan-heavy plans also wait longer in CPU run queues, causing lock hold times, connection pool exhaustion, and sporadic timeouts. Maintenance tasks (auto-vacuum, statistics refresh, checkpoint, log flushing) compete for already scarce CPU, so short stalls ripple into user-visible slowdowns and variance in response times.

Causally, sub-optimal schema and missing or misaligned indexes compel the optimizer to choose resource-hungry plans that read and process excess rows; this inflates per-query CPU demand. The aggregate effect of many such inefficient executions drives CPU Resource Anomaly. Once cores are saturated, the scheduler elongates every CPU quantum, further magnifying the cost of each scan, join, and sort. High CPU pressure delays background tasks that might otherwise mitigate bloat or refresh statistics, locking the system into a feedback loop where degraded physical design and compute starvation reinforce one another, ultimately depressing throughput and threatening stability under both transactional and analytical workloads.

entry.error_class: Class 42 - Syntax Error or Access Rule Violation
entry.cause_analysis: The failure is typically associated with unsupported syntax, invalid statement structure, or feature usage that the target engine version cannot execute as written.
entry.solution_guidance: Validate SQL syntax, target-engine compatibility, statement shape, and whether the feature is supported under the current engine version or execution context.
